schoolReviews.review: This school is amazing. Definitely has some of the best teachers you can find. Mr. Abejuela has a pull-up bar in his classroom and challenges students not only mentally but physically. Mr. Dissalvo always presents both sides to any argument so we could form our own opinions and even let us debate in the middle of class often. Mr. Wendel wrote a song and sang it with his guitar for our class at the end of the year, it was hilarious! Mr. Graham was an amazing science teacher and made learning about moles and the periodic table interesting. Ms. Alvarez was the most passionate teacher who ensured that each and every student had the help they needed to pass her class. Finally, Mr. Rivero always had a smile on his face and being in his class, even during Saturday school, brought happiness.

Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Merced High School and graduated in 2011. I was able to experience a variety of great teachers and learned skills I wasn't aware some schools don't have as a standard. They prepare students for jobs with mock interviews, resumes, cover letters and we covered a course on how to get into stocks. There was cooking and a home living elective class as well as many others. The school was also available to special need students and even though their classes were separate, they encouraged us all to have healthy interactions with eachother. So we'd have rallies and special events together. Another good benefit to the student is that the school has an open campus policy that gave Juniors and Seniors privileges to leave the campus during lunch as an insentive and if your academics are poor then you'd get the privilege revoked. If you are doing poorly in school, we have great counselors who care about your academics as long as you show an interest in wanting to succeed. They are also attentive to last year students, so that they are all prepared to graduate or even move on to other career paths. I received all these benefits as a student before the new high school was built and there was about 30 student average per teacher, so I can only imagine how great of an education these students can get going to Merced High School now with the new gym being built and a much more breathable school environment.

This school is simple and a bit old compared to the nearby schools. It has some problems such as old rooms and such stuff but overall appearance wise this school is okay. I like how the original Merced High School is the best overall school wise in the county. This school could improve by having more school spirit and landscape. In the old days this school actually had flowers!

schoolReviews.review: My two children are in the MONTESSORI PROGRAM at John Muir, and this reviews focuses specifically on that program. I have been amazed at the level of both social AND academic growth of my kids since they have entered this program. The nature of the program teaches them to be self-motivated, curious and excited about learning, and most importantly, kind and compassionate. My kids can progress at their own pace, learn an amazing amount about different cultures, and also learn a deep respect for their peers and the diversity in their community. I cannot recommend the Montessori program more highly. The program is moving to Ada Givens in the Fall of 2017.

Before my son transferred to John Muir he was cast as a problem child. When he started 4th grade at John Muir I went to talk to his teacher regarding his "behavioral problems" she could not believe that he had ever had a problem. Not only was he at the top of the class academically, she told us he was kind, helpful, respectful, and a perfect student. She was flabbergasted at how he could be seen as a problem. He continued his elementary education at John Muir and did wonderfully. My daughter now attends first grade their and we are still just as pleased. The staff is very friendly, helpful, and professional. The teachers are excellent and the homework that my kids bring home is above what is expected for the grade. I know that the state scores are low but I believe that this has to do with a lot of the students being ESL students still learning English. The district is in a low income area but the school does not reflect this at all. I am proud to be a parent of a John Muir student.

This school has wonderful and caring teachers, administrators and staff. The principal is first-rate and he gives his staff the tools to do their jobs effectively. It is one of the oldest schools in the Merced County School District but the school seems more contemporary because it is academically and technologically on the forefront such as offering Montessori classes in grades 1-3 and having iPads in some of the classrooms. The one area of improvement would be to have more field trips which is often a function of budgetary constraints. However, even trips to local museums and other sites (which is more economical) would enhance student learning and engender greater appreciation for the community.

I have four children attending John Muir. They have attended since Kinder. I have always spoke so highly of their staff, teaCher, and principle until this year. Some of the teachers there lack their position as a teacher, the principle now just has little interest for what the students need. The parents are not allowed on campus, how do we maintain teacher parent communication. I find my kids believing they have more independence now since we dont get notices of mark, failing grades, and the understanding of what our children are learning. I wish i could say more good but i being lying. The only thing i can say is all my kids are doing very well, and advancing, they have good programs of education there they just need to pull together as a team. Its crazy sometimes because they are short staff,

My son went to this school for a month and a half, K teacher he first had was great and really understood our sons educational and behavioral needs. Then he was switched classes with out no parent or student notifacation, and created enough problems to tranfer him from schools.

John Muir is an excellent school with an experienced dedicated staff and one of the best principals in the county. My son is in 2nd grade and has access to both a chess club and a science club and is challenged to do his best every week. I can recommend this school without reservations.

schoolReviews.review: My daughter was assaulted several times and Ada Givens Elementary School in Merced, CA swept our complaints under the rug. Teachers give low scores at the beginning to later give higher scores giving false impression ofacademic progress thanks to their teaching. Teachers did not treat my child fairly and theCalifornia Department of Education routinely dismiss our complaints. School Principal is rude. Students disrupt teacher talking in class, skip class and strain the patience of teachers with rampant absences costing the school Federal attendance funds and causing teacher burnout. Celebrations involve loud music speakers pointed towards performing students causing Tinnitus(damage to ear nerves). My child scored near perfect score in IQ tests and transferred to a better school.

My child is currently in the fourth grade and has been at the school for three years. While Merced itself is socioeconomically problematic and the backgrounds of some of the students must be challenging, I can’t help but be impressed by this school. The staff is friendly and helpful and the teachers are amazing. Our experience as parents of a child at Ada Givens has been excellent so far. My child has loved every teacher he’s had and feels safe, happy, and motivated to learn here.
This school gave my kid hotdog water for lunch.

I have two boys that were enrolled in this school after moving to our new house, I went into the office and enrolled both my boys age 5 and age 7 one in kinder and the other in 2nd grade. I walked them both to there classes this morning along with the secretary and we all had a talk about my 7 year old walking to my 5 year's class and waiting for there pick up I was also told how my children would not be allowed to leave that class until there ride picked them up, However when my sister arrived to pick them up at 2:20pm no one knew where my kids were, the school did not even notify of my kids being lost and my sister was by the office staff o well she called me and told me what was going on I called the school and they acted like no big deal!! I did notify the police thank GOD my kids were found after walking home alone at age 5 and 7 more than 6 blocks away from the school! This school is a joke if you want your kids to be safe then this school is not right for you!!!!!!!
I feel this school has a great staff and a great ASSETS program after school hours.

We have loved this school. Three of our children attend this school. The parent involvment is really poor though but that is no reflection on the school, more the parents lack of care for thier kids. The teachers have been fabulous, especially Mrs. Pino ion 2nd grade. The principal and office staff are great.

schoolReviews.review: Hello to whomever is reading this, I went to this school(OLM) since preschool to eighth grade and now I'm a parent ironic huh. In 7th grade I went to a local public school for a month. Wow OLM just blows away any other school , the teachers are fantastic and take the time to teach the material. the school has received many awards. If you're worried about the price don't worry the education will pay off.

It is a close knit school. Most kids have grow up with each from kindergarten. The close bond that they form with one another continues to grow through high school and beyond. Students and alumni also have done a lot for our community. I feel my kids not only got an awesome education but were taught to be friendly, caring people that give to others.
I have had the best experience at OLM and sonhave my children. I would recommend OLM to anyone

OLM is a fantastic school which provides excellent preparation for High School. I have sent 3 children through the school and they are currently at the top of their respective classes in both high school and college. The teachers are terrific and really care about the kids as individuals. The discipline (i.e. no cell phone during school) may seem like an anti-social "prison-like" requirement for some, but it is actually an excellent exercise in self-control for the kids. My kids are as social as any and have learned key lessons like being kind to others, tolerance,respect, and teamwork- as well as being really well prepared academically. They have excellent sports programs too. The tuition is lower than lessor programs in the surrounding areas and a tremendous value. Also-you do not have to be Catholic to attend and in fact many students are not and are totally comfortable there. I am thrilled with our family's experience at the school and I would highly recommend it if you are looking for an excellent, individualized, academic and athletic experience in a structured, kind and loving environment for your child.
Terrible teachers, make students feel like they're living in a prison. No social contact or exposure to friends and family.

Great school, I highly recommend it. One of the toughest academic programs in Merced. Safe environment with well-structured curriculum and supportive teachers. On another note, I read a disappointing experience on here and it sounds like that parent is simply bitter and has some personal grudge against OLM. As a UCLA PhD graduate with a degree in Psychology, cliques will develop anywhere and are a natural part of growing up. Parents should take more responsibility, if the mere existence of cliques are causing 'psychological damage,' it's time to think again in terms of what really is psychologically damaging your child. And it cliques not clicks.
